faq.q: What does path of least resistance mean?
faq.a: It means the option that takes the least effort, conflict, or discomfort. As an idiom, it often describes choosing what’s easiest rather than what’s best.

faq.q: Where does the phrase come from?
faq.a: It comes from nature and physics, where water flows downhill along the easiest route and electric current is described as favoring the path with the lowest resistance.

faq.q: Is taking the path of least resistance always bad?
faq.a: No. It’s a trap when it helps you avoid growth or hard conversations, but it can be wise when it means working with your strengths or dropping friction that doesn’t matter.

faq.q: Why do people naturally choose the easiest option?
faq.a: Our minds try to save effort, so habits, defaults, and short-term comfort tend to win. Knowing this makes it easier to design better defaults.

faq.q: How can I use the path of least resistance to build habits?
faq.a: Make good habits easier by removing steps, and add friction to unhelpful ones. Deciding in advance and starting with tiny steps also helps.

faq.q: How do I know if resistance is worth pushing through?
faq.a: Ask whether the discomfort helps you grow and moves you toward your values. If it does, it’s worth facing; if it’s just friction, you can remove it.
